description: Mustang Customs surpasses Rs 9 billion annual revenue targets in just 3 months  myRepublica
publisher.title: myRepublica
full_article:
KATHMANDU, Nov 1: The Mustang Customs Office (MCO), located at the Korala border crossing between Nepal and China, contributed customs revenue worth Rs 11.45 billion during the first three and a half months of the current Fiscal Year (FY).

(adsbygoogle = window.adsbygoogle || []).push({});

The amount of public revenue surpassed the MCO’s annual target by Rs 2.45 billion just in one-fourth of the period. The customs was given a target of revenue worth Rs 9 billion for the current FY. Last FY, the MCO collected customs revenue of Rs 6.92 billion.

According to Customs Officer Amindra Singh, goods worth Rs 26.01 billion were imported from China via the Korala border crossing as of Friday starting the FY 2026/27 in mid-July. Likewise, goods valued at Rs 286.3 million were exported from Nepal to China through this border.

Related story Birgunj customs mobilizes Rs 161 billion in revenue

Mustang-Korala has lately emerged as an alternative to the land-based bilateral trade with China since Bhotekoshi-Trishuli flood hit the main trading gateway on August 26. As per the MCO, 6,501 Electric Vehicles (EVs) imported from China received their customs clearance.

The MCO had collected Rs 8.33 billion in revenue before Dashain i.e. mid-October. In the past 18 days following the festival, the customs office collected an additional Rs 3.12 billion.

The MCO further reported that Chinese goods worth Rs 10.40 billion were imported into Nepal via the Korala crossing before Dashain, with an additional Rs 6.70 billion worth of goods imported after the festival.

According to MCO Chief Singh, both exports and imports through the Korala border have increased due to the complete closure of the Rasuwagadhi and Tatopani border points. Following a devastating flood in the Bhote Koshi of ​​Rasuwa, the route was diverted, resulting in the import of goods contained in hundreds of containers through the Korala border.

The festival-focused goods including ready-made garments, cosmetics, electronic devices, industrial raw materials, food grains, fruits and electric vehicles were among the main imported goods. The government brought the northern Nepal-China Korala border point into full operation in mid-September of the last FY.

publisher.title: Khabarhub
full_article:
KATHMANDU: The 11th edition of the Nepal International Trade Fair will be held in Kathmandu from December 3 to 7, with the aim of promoting Nepal’s international trade.

Organised by the Federation of Nepalese Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FNCCI) with government support, the fair will feature participation from Nepal, China, India, Pakistan, Bangladesh and Bhutan.

The event aims to boost exports of products identified as priorities under the Nepal Trade Integration Strategy, including cardamom, tea, ginger, handicrafts, pashmina, and medicinal and aromatic herbs.

At a press conference held in Kathmandu on Sunday, organisers said that more than 200 stalls would be set up to showcase domestic and international goods and services.

Handicraft products and electric vehicles are expected to be the major attractions of the fair. Discussions on promoting bilateral trade and investment will also be held during the event. The organisers expect around 100,000 visitors to attend.

According to the FNCCI, the fair is expected to attract foreign investment and technology to Nepal, promote Nepali products in international markets and contribute to the country’s overall economic development.

title: 43 disaster incidents reported across Nepal, 13 injured - Khabarhub
description: 43 disaster incidents reported across Nepal, 13 injured  Khabarhub
publisher.title: Khabarhub
full_article:
KATHMANDU: At least 13 people have been injured in 43 disaster-related incidents reported across the country in recent days, with property damage estimated at Rs 940,000.

According to the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority (NDRRMA), the incidents included landslides, heavy rainfall, floods, fires, snakebites, animal attacks and snowfall.

Landslides accounted for the highest number of incidents, with 17 cases reported nationwide, said Ram Bahadur KC, spokesperson for the authority.

Similarly, seven incidents were triggered by heavy rainfall, while five cases each of fire and flooding were recorded. There were also four incidents each involving snakebites and animal attacks, along with one snowfall-related incident during the reporting period, KC said.

Some of the injured are receiving treatment at local hospitals, while others have been referred to hospitals in neighbouring districts for further medical care.

The authority said rescue, relief and response operations were underway in coordination with relevant agencies in the affected areas. It is also collecting further details on casualties and property damage.

title: Nepali Congress Leader Pradip Poudel Claims Democratic Ideology Accepted - Ratopati
description: Nepali Congress Leader Pradip Poudel Claims Democratic Ideology Accepted  Ratopati
publisher.title: Ratopati
full_article:
Pokhara. Nepali Congress General Secretary Pradip Poudel has claimed that the multi-party democratic ideology put forward by the Congress has become universally acceptable in Nepal's politics. Addressing a program in Pokhara for the assumption of office by Kaski Constituency No. 1 of the Nepali Congress, he said that power and the number of seats in parliament are temporary, but the victory of ideology is permanent.

Hinting at the ruling party RSP, he commented that despite making many claims and propaganda, they have not been able to show results. 'The new friends who came talked about many things. But they did nothing,' he said. 'The multi-party democratic system in Nepal is a topic that the Nepali Congress initiated a debate on in Nepali society. Today, all those who did not accept that ideology have had to return to this path.'

He claimed that communists, royalists who rejected democratic methods yesterday, and even the new parties of today have been forced to come to the Congress's policies and methods. 'Communists did not accept this system, nor did the royalists,' he added. 'Now, the new friends who have come have also reached power through this system. Therefore, there is no situation where anyone does not accept the Congress's ideology today.'

General Secretary Poudel said that the influence of ideology is greater than the equation of power and the mathematics of parliament. 'In politics, who reaches power, whose numbers are more in parliament, that is not permanent. Whose ideology is accepted by society and the country, that is important. Today, the ideology of the Nepali Congress has become universally acceptable in Nepal's politics,' he says.

Poudel said that in Congress, the past glory alone will not shape the present and future. He emphasized the need to hold onto the core principles of democratic socialism propounded by BP Koirala and make its content contemporary. He, who has just come out for district tours after completing the general convention, said that those defeated in the party's internal elections should also be taken along.

'Since Congress is a university of politics, it will teach culture and methods,' he said. 'Those who win must be able to take those who lose along with them for their entire tenure, and those who lose must also accept the technical results and cooperate in building the organization.'

title: Nepal Premier League Management Questioned Over Match Delays and Field Conditions - Ratopati
description: Nepal Premier League Management Questioned Over Match Delays and Field Conditions  Ratopati
publisher.title: Ratopati
full_article:
Kathmandu. The controversy over the condition of the field in Saturday's Nepal Premier League (NPL) match has also raised questions about the management aspect of match operations.

The first match between Chitwan Rhinos and Lumbini Lions was canceled due to the wet ground caused by rain. After that, the second match between Biratnagar Kings and Sudurpaschim Royals was repeatedly scheduled. The toss, initially set for 5 PM, was announced to be at 7:25 PM. The match still couldn't start, and the toss time was postponed again. Finally, the toss took place after 9 PM, and the match was limited to five overs.

Does postponing the toss time repeatedly after announcing the match time make sense? This incident has raised a significant question. Is this postponement within the rules? And how long can the match wait, considering player safety when the ground is not fit for play?

In cricket, if a match cannot start at the scheduled time due to rain, low light, or ground conditions, the toss and start times can be postponed. However, a specific procedure and timeline must be followed.

Clause 13.4 of the ICC's Men's T20 International Playing Conditions deals with the toss. According to this provision, the captain must toss between 15 to 30 minutes before the scheduled or rescheduled start time of the match. In other words, the rules allow for the rescheduling of the match time.

This means that the toss time is not unchangeable. If there is a possibility of the ground conditions improving, the umpires can determine a new match time after inspection. They can also set a time for re-inspection if necessary. Postponing the inspection time and postponing the final deadline for the match to start are not the same thing.

The match deadline, minimum overs, and time available to complete the match are determined according to the tournament's applicable playing conditions. The organizers must provide a clear basis from their regulations on whether a match can be played after the deadline has passed.

On Saturday, after the decision to play the match between Biratnagar and Sudurpaschim in five overs, the toss was announced for 7:25 PM and the first ball at 7:41 PM. However, the toss did not happen at the scheduled time. Although Biratnagar captain Sandeep Lamichhane came to the field, Sudurpaschim captain Dipendra Singh Airee did not. Following this, a discussion took place between the team's coach Misbah Ul Haq, manager Sunil Thapa, Airee, Cricket Association of Nepal (CAN) secretary Paras Khadka, and match referee Wendell Labuschagne.

Sudurpaschim expressed dissatisfaction regarding the wet outfield and player safety. At 8:54 PM, after Sudurpaschim informed they were ready to play, the toss time was set for 9 PM and the match start time for 9:15 PM. Finally, the toss took place at 9:05 PM, and the match started at 9:15 PM.

The scheduled time for the first ball of the five-over match was 7:41 PM. However, the match started at 9:15 PM. This means the match started 94 minutes later than the initially scheduled time.

This was not just a matter of a normal rain delay. The question arises as to on what rule and authority the decision was made to start the match even after the operational deadline had passed. The official tournament source of the NPL had indicated 7:41 PM as the final time to start a five-over match for Saturday's game. The arrangement was to ensure that both teams could play at least five overs each.

If 7:41 PM was indeed the final deadline according to the tournament rules, then the decision to start the match at 9:15 PM later that night needs a formal explanation. However, if the organizers set a new deadline after discussions with the players and teams and after the umpires' inspection, then the NPL rule that permitted this must also be made public.

Even considering the ICC's T20 International rules, there is a provision to reschedule the start time of the match. However, this does not automatically nullify the tournament's minimum playing time and other conditions. It is also not the case that all ICC international match operating conditions automatically apply to the NPL. Therefore, to reach a final conclusion, it is necessary to examine the official 'Playing Conditions' and tournament regulations of the third edition of the NPL.

In international cricket, there are many instances of postponing toss times due to rain, repeatedly inspecting the ground, and ultimately canceling matches. However, an exact similar incident where a match was conducted after the start time deadline, following lengthy discussions, as seen in the NPL, has not been encountered so far.

According to Clauses 2.7 and 2.8 of the ICC's T20 International Playing Conditions, the umpires jointly decide whether the ground, weather, and light are suitable for play.

If the ground is wet to the extent that a bowler cannot get a foothold, a fielder cannot run freely, or a batter finds it difficult to take runs, it can be considered dangerous or unfair. In such a situation, the umpires have the authority to not allow the match to start or to stop an ongoing match. They can make decisions in consultation with the match referee. However, the final decision on whether the ground is fit for play rests with the umpires.

Therefore, it cannot be said that the match referee acted against the rules simply by deciding to postpone the time. However, if the match was conducted after the final deadline had passed, the basis and procedure for it must be clarified.

title: Influence of Cyclone Arnab diminishing, weather improving - The Rising Nepal
description: Influence of Cyclone Arnab diminishing, weather improving  The Rising Nepal
publisher.title: The Rising Nepal
full_article:
Kathmandu, Nov 1: The effects of the low pressure area situated near western Nepal, which is a remnant of Cyclone Arnab, are subsiding, and the weather is progressively getting better.

According to the Weather Forecasting Division, currently, the mountainous regions of the country, including Lumbini province, are generally cloudy, while the remainder of the country experiences partial cloudiness.

Light rain is occurring in certain areas of Bagmati, Gandaki, Lumbini, and Karnali regions. The division forecasts that this afternoon, the country will be partly cloudy, with a chance of light rain and snowfall in one or two locations in the Himalayan and hilly regions.

Tonight, the weather will remain partly cloudy across the country. There is a likelihood of light rain and snowfall in one or two areas of the Himalayan and hilly sections of Gandaki, Karnali, and Sudurpashchim provinces. (RSS)
